c.tagline: The Mile High City where craft beer, big skies, and the Rockies meet.

taxi.fareNote: Cabs are metered but scarce for street hailing; most visitors book Uber or Lyft, which are widely available.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number connecting to police, fire, and ambulance across the United States.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.RiNo (River North Art District): River North Art District Denver murals

avoid.reason: Caution around parts of downtown/16th St and Union Station at night — property crime

hood_desc: Denver's historic core and Lower Downtown (LoDo), centered on Union Station, Larimer Square, and Coors Field; the most walkable base for first-timers, packed with breweries, rooftop bars, and chef-driven restaurants in restored 19th-century warehouses.

The River North Art District, a former industrial zone reborn as Denver's creative hub, covered in large-scale murals and lined with art studios, craft breweries, distilleries, and buzzy new-American eateries; best for travelers who want galleries and nightlife with an edge.

A dense, historic residential district just east of downtown around the gold-domed Colorado State Capitol and Civic Center Park, home to grand Victorian mansions, the Denver Art Museum, and a lively, affordable bar and live-music scene; popular with younger and budget travelers.

An upscale shopping and dining enclave built around Cherry Creek North's boutiques and the Cherry Creek Shopping Center, plus the Denver Botanic Gardens nearby; suits travelers wanting luxury retail, spas, and refined restaurants in a polished setting.

The Lower Highlands (LoHi), a hip, walkable neighborhood across the river from downtown with skyline views from the pedestrian bridge, Victorian streets, and one of the city's densest clusters of popular restaurants, rooftop patios, and cocktail bars.
lodging: The Maven Hotel at Dairy Block

water.note: Tap water is safe and tastes good, sourced largely from Rocky Mountain snowmelt.

transit.hours: Light rail and most bus routes run roughly 4am to 1am, with reduced weekend frequency; the A Line airport train runs 24/7 every 15 minutes.
transit.note: RTD operates Denver's light rail, commuter rail, and bus network across the metro area. The system uses two fare zones, Local and Airport, with a discounted MyRide stored-value option.
transit.pay: Pay via the RTD MyRide card, the RTD Mobile Tickets app, or tap a contactless bank card or phone at rail validators and on buses. A 3-hour Local pass is $2.75 (or $2.42 with MyRide), a Day Pass is $5.50, and trips to or from the airport require a $10 Airport Pass.

train: RTD A Line commuter rail to the airport

transit.m: RTD A Line commuter train to Union Station (37 min, every 15 min, 24/7)

tip.r: ~15-20% at restaurants is standard; round up or add a dollar or two for bars, taxis, and coffee.

food.name: Green chile smothered burrito
food.desc: A flour tortilla stuffed with pork, beans or eggs then drowned in Colorado green chile, a pork-and-roasted-Pueblo-chile gravy, and melted cheese.

places.name: El Taco de Mexico
places.note: James Beard America's Classic; four decades of the city's benchmark green chile over a smothered burrito.

places.name: Brewery Bar II
places.note: Won the Denver Post 2025 best green chile nod; smothered burritos and chile rellenos since 1972.

places.name: Santiago's
places.note: Homegrown chain famous for a fiery green chile locals buy by the quart to take home.

food.name: Denver omelette
food.desc: The city's namesake breakfast: eggs folded around diced ham, green bell pepper, onion and cheddar, usually served with hash browns and toast.

places.name: Sam's No. 3
places.note: Diner descended from a 1927 Greek-run lunch counter; huge omelettes and a green chile to smother them.

places.name: Pete's Kitchen
places.note: Colfax Avenue griddle open around the clock; the classic late-night Denver omelette.

places.name: The Delectable Egg
places.note: Breakfast specialist that has been doing egg dishes in Denver since 1982.

food.name: Rocky Mountain trout
food.desc: Colorado rainbow or brook trout, usually pan-fried whole in cornmeal or butter with lemon and almonds; the mountain-state fish course.

places.name: Buckhorn Exchange
places.note: Denver's oldest restaurant, open since 1893, serving Rocky Mountain trout under 500-plus mounted trophies.

places.name: The Fort
places.note: Adobe fort replica in the foothills; historic Colorado menu built on trout, game and Bent's Fort recipes.

places.name: Urban Farmer
places.note: Oxford Hotel steakhouse that sources Colorado trout and produce from nearby ranches and farms.

food.name: Colorado bison and elk
food.desc: Lean, grass-fed bison steaks and elk medallions from Colorado ranches, usually served rare with a berry or chile sauce and mountain vegetables.

places.name: Buckhorn Exchange
places.note: Game-house menu of bison, elk, quail and rattlesnake in a 19th-century saloon room.

places.name: The Fort
places.note: Sells more bison than almost any US restaurant; the buffalo steaks are the reason to drive out.

places.name: Denver ChopHouse
places.note: Old rail-depot steakhouse by Coors Field with bison on the grill alongside the beef.

food.name: Rocky Mountain oysters
food.desc: Sliced, breaded and deep-fried bull calf testicles served with horseradish cocktail sauce; a Colorado ranching tradition and a genuine dare dish.

places.name: Buckhorn Exchange
places.note: The definitive Denver plate of Rocky Mountain oysters, on the menu here since the 1890s.

places.name: The Fort
places.note: Serves them as historic frontier fare with a straight face and good sauce.

places.name: Denver ChopHouse
places.note: Keeps them on the appetiser list for the ballpark crowd next door.

food.name: Chile relleno
food.desc: A whole roasted Pueblo or poblano chile stuffed with cheese, egg-battered, fried crisp and then smothered in the same green chile as the burritos.

places.name: Brewery Bar II
places.note: Its crispy chile rellenos are as celebrated as the green chile they arrive under.

places.name: Chakas Mexican Restaurant
places.note: Strip-mall favourite on East Evans doing smothered plates from breakfast through dinner.

places.name: El Taco de Mexico
places.note: Counter-service relleno done the old way, best eaten at the bar watching the cooks.

food.name: Colorado craft beer
food.desc: Denver is a founding city of American craft brewing; expect big hoppy IPAs, barrel-aged stouts and the Great American Beer Festival each autumn.

places.name: Great Divide Brewery and Roadhouse
places.note: Denver's first microbrewery, founded 1994; the Blake Street taproom pours a dozen of its beers.

places.name: Wynkoop Brewing Co.
places.note: Colorado's first brewpub, opened 1988, still pouring in a historic warehouse with pool upstairs.

places.name: Denver Beer Co.
places.note: Platte Street patio brewery with rotating seasonals; a relaxed introduction to the local scene.

food.name: Colorado whiskey
food.desc: High-altitude distilling took off here, led by Stranahan's Rocky Mountain single malt and Leopold Bros; drunk neat or in a Colorado old fashioned.

places.name: Stranahan's Colorado Whiskey
places.note: Distillery tours and tastings at the Kalamath Street home of the state's original single malt.

places.name: Williams and Graham
places.note: Bookshop-front speakeasy consistently ranked among the best cocktail bars in the country.

places.name: Wynkoop Brewing Co.
places.note: Pairs Colorado spirits with its own beer in a proper old Denver bar room.

landmarks: Red Rocks Amphitheatre
A world-famous open-air concert venue set among massive red sandstone formations just outside the city.
Denver Union Station
A beautifully restored 1914 Beaux-Arts train station with a giant illuminated "UNION STATION" sign.
Colorado State Capitol
Topped with a genuine gold-leaf dome, it sits exactly one mile above sea level with a marked step to prove it.
Denver Art Museum
The angular, titanium-clad Hamilton Building is one of the boldest pieces of contemporary architecture in the city.
Denver Botanic Gardens
Themed gardens and striking modern greenhouse architecture make this a colorful year-round photo destination.
Denver Museum of Nature and Science
A landmark museum overlooking City Park with the Rocky Mountains as a dramatic backdrop.
Larimer Square
Denver's oldest and most charmingly historic block, lined with Victorian-era buildings and string lights.
Molly Brown House Museum
The preserved Victorian home of "The Unsinkable" Molly Brown, a Titanic survivor and Denver icon.
16th Street Mall
Denver's pedestrian downtown corridor lined with shops and views toward the mountains at its western end.
Denver Zoo
A century-old zoo in City Park known for its historic entrance pavilion and diverse animal exhibits.

train.note: One long-distance train serves Denver Union Station: Amtrak's California Zephyr, once a day in each direction between Chicago and Emeryville for San Francisco. The westbound climb out of Denver through the Moffat Tunnel and Glenwood Canyon is one of the great scenic rail rides in North America, so book the Sightseer Lounge side of the day. In winter Amtrak also runs the weekend Winter Park Express ski train up to the resort. Union Station is the hub for RTD's commuter rail, including the A Line out to Denver International Airport in about 37 minutes. Canada and Mexico are both far too distant for any through train.

bus.note: No international coaches - Denver is over 500 miles from the nearest border. The Colorado Department of Transportation's Bustang network (https://ridebustang.com/) is the workhorse for the state, running from Union Station's underground bus concourse north to Fort Collins, south to Colorado Springs and Pueblo, and west over the Rockies to Glenwood Springs and Grand Junction, with Outrider routes reaching Gunnison, Alamosa and Craig. Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/), Burlington Trailways (https://www.burlingtontrailways.com/) and Express Arrow also use the same concourse. Bustang fares are low and reservations are worth making for ski-season weekends.

ferry.note: Denver is a mile-high inland city roughly 1,000 miles from any ocean and has no ferry services at all; the only boats are recreational craft on reservoirs such as Chatfield and Cherry Creek.

half.name: Rocky Mountain National Park
half.blurb: High-alpine park with Trail Ridge Road climbing above 12,000 feet, elk herds, and glacial lakes near Estes Park.

half.name: Boulder
half.blurb: College town at the foot of the Flatirons rock formations, with a pedestrian Pearl Street mall and hiking trails.

half.name: Garden of the Gods
half.blurb: Red sandstone rock garden near Colorado Springs with towering formations set against a Pikes Peak backdrop.

half.name: Georgetown
half.blurb: Preserved 19th-century silver-mining town in the mountains, reachable by a scenic historic narrow-gauge railway loop.
